regions.justification: Official survey data is 60 days stale while hospital admissions have risen 50% over the last 14 days, and resource allocation sits 35% below the regional average. This region is at high risk of an undetected, escalating outbreak.

Survey data is over a month and a half old and admissions are up 45%, while funding and vaccine stock are roughly 28% below average. The combination of stale reporting and rising caseload suggests a developing outbreak that official channels have not yet captured.
The latest survey is 42 days old and admissions have climbed 38% in two weeks, with resource levels 20% below average. This region shows all three blind-spot signals at once.
Survey data is stale and admissions are trending upward, but resource allocation is close to the regional average. The emerging trend warrants attention even though capacity is less constrained.
Admissions are up 22% and the survey is 39 days old. Resource levels are slightly below average, suggesting a moderate and partially-resourced risk that should be monitored.
